To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic diversification of DENV serotypes in Mexico is associated with a complex evolutionary pattern that is characterized by the coexistence of multiple genotypes, which may be a consequence of multiple introduction events of DENV strains from different geographic regions.

(1) the genetic diversification of DENV serotypes 1, 3, and 4 in Mexico is driven by the introduction of novel genotypes, (2) DENV serotype 1, genotype I and serotype 3, genotype II, have been circulating in Mexico since 2000, and (3) the genetic diversifications of DENV serotype II and serotype IV have been driven by the introduction and circulation of novel genotypes.
dengue virus serotype and genotype evolution in Mexico is associated with the introduction of novel genotypes and the emergence of novel genotypes.
